sec: Subacute IE: symptoms, signs, emboli, laboratory features, Janeway vs Osler

items.q: Which background is printed at the top of the subacute-IE case?
opts: Congenital heart disease with rheumatic fever in childhood, treated for RHD
Recent dental extraction in a normal valve
Prosthetic aortic valve replaced last month
Central venous catheter in a patient on chemotherapy
items.exp: 'H/o : · CHD, + Rheumatic fever in childhood, treatment for RHD.' (Book p1049)

items.q: Symptoms versus signs — match — 1) Symptoms 2) Signs … A) New onset or worsening cardiac murmur, macro- and microembolic events, splenomegaly/clubbing B) Fever with chills for 2-3 months, anorexia, weight loss, fatigue, myalgia
items.exp: 'Symptoms : Fever with chills × 2-3 months, Anorexia, weight loss, Fatigue, myalgia'; 'Signs : New onset cardiac murmur / worsening of an existing murmur, macroembolic events, microembolic events, Splenomegaly / clubbing'. (Book p1049)

items.q: How long is the fever printed as lasting in the subacute case?
Embolic phenomena — match — 1) Macroembolic 2) Microembolic … A) Petechiae and splinter haemorrhage B) Stroke, ACS, retinal occlusion
items.exp: 'macroembolic events : stroke, ACS, retinal occlusion'; 'microembolic events : Petechiae and splinter hemorrhage'. (Book p1049)

items.q: Immunological manifestations — match — 1) Osler nodes 2) Roth spots 3) Positive rheumatoid factor … A) Retinal endothelial vasculitis with a pale centre and surrounding erythema B) Tender nodules of the finger and toe pulps C) Positive in about half of cases
items.exp: 'manifestation a/w vasculitis : · Osler nodes, RF positivity, Roth spots : Retinal endothelial vasculitis — Pale centre with surrounding erythema'; 'Rheumatoid factor +ve (50% cases)'. (Book p1049)

items.q: In what proportion of cases is rheumatoid factor positive in subacute IE?
Proteinuria and microscopic haematuria are printed in what proportion of cases?
items.exp: '· Proteinuria and microscopic hematuria (50% cases)'. (Book p1049)

items.q: Laboratory features — match — 1) Anaemia 2) White cells 3) Acute phase … A) Raised ESR and CRP B) Normocytic C) Raised count
items.exp: 'Laboratory features : · Anemia (Normocytic), · ↑ WBC, · ↑ ESR, · CRP'. (Book p1049)

items.q: Janeway lesions versus Osler nodes — match — 1) Site 2) Size and shape 3) Tenderness 4) Course 5) Type of endocarditis 6) Culture 7) Histology … A) Nodules 1 mm to > 1 cm; tender; hours to days; subacute; usually negative; vasculitis B) Macules of variable size and irregular shape; non-tender; days to weeks; acute; usually positive; septic microemboli
items.exp: Janeway: soles, palms, thenar and hypothenar eminences and plantar surfaces of the toes; macules of variable size and irregular shape; not tender; days to weeks; acute; culture positive; septic microemboli. Osler: finger and toe tips, pulp, thenar and hypothenar eminences; nodules 1 mm to > 1 cm; tender; hours to days; subacute; culture negative; vasculitis. (Book p1049)

items.q: Where are Janeway lesions printed as occurring?
opts: Soles, palms, thenar and hypothenar eminences, plantar surfaces of the toes
Finger and toe tips and pulps only
items.exp: 'Janeway lesion — Soles, palms, thenar and hypothenar eminences, plantar surfaces of the toe'. (Book p1049)

items.q: What size range is printed for Osler nodes?
items.exp: 'Osler node — Nodules of 1 mm to > 1 cm'. (Book p1049)

items.q: Judge the comparison table: I Janeway lesions are non-tender macules of acute endocarditis with positive cultures. II Osler nodes are tender nodules of subacute endocarditis with negative cultures.
items.exp: Janeway column: macules, non-tender, days to weeks, acute, culture positive, septic microemboli. Osler column: nodules, tender, hours to days, subacute, culture negative, vasculitis. (Book p1049)

items.q: A febrile patient with a murmur has tender nodules on the finger pulps and a negative blood culture. Which lesion and endocarditis type does the table indicate?
items.exp: Tender nodules of the pulps with negative cultures are the Osler-node column, linked to subacute endocarditis. (Book p1049)
